purpose: Extend the Noether research/publication lane with scholarly and policy anchors, reviewer authority checklists, and a decision framework for distinguishing natural-language translation lanes, zonal/interlanguage work, constructed-language pilots, and computational pivots.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Centre for Research and Documentation on World Language Problems
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Establishes interlinguistics, language policy, and linguistic justice as an existing research ecosystem.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: CED description of Language Problems and Language Planning
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Journal witness for multilingual scholarship on language problems, planning, and policy.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Federico Gobbo, Introduction to Interlinguistics
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Book-length scholarly orientation for interlinguistics and planned-language study.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Dialect, language, nation: 50 years on
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Anchor for separating selection, codification, elaboration/function, implementation/diffusion, and acceptance questions.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Robert L. Cooper, Language Planning and Social Change
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Anchor for status, corpus, and acquisition planning and for the social purposes of language planning.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Bernard Spolsky, Language Policy
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Anchor for distinguishing practices, beliefs or ideologies, and management decisions.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Grant Goodall, Constructed Languages
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Recent scholarly overview treating constructed languages as legitimate linguistic research objects.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Nathan Sanders, Constructed languages in the classroom
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Pedagogy anchor for constructed languages as classroom tools, distinct from community or canonical authority.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Language Invention in Linguistics Pedagogy
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Book-level witness for invented languages as university pedagogy practice.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: UNESCO languages in education
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Education-policy anchor for mother-language and multilingual education, inclusion, and learner comprehension.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: UNESCO multilingual education article
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Policy anchor for multilingual education as a quality and inclusion issue.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Rights anchor for language, culture, education, self-determination, and community authority.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: UN declaration on minority rights
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Rights anchor for linguistic minorities and language use without discrimination.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: UNESCO OER Recommendation
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Open-education anchor for licensing, localization, capacity-building, and reusable educational materials.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: CARE Principles
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Governance anchor for collective benefit, authority to control, responsibility, and ethics.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: TRUST Code
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Ethics anchor for avoiding extractive research partnerships and one-way authority claims.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: FAIR Principles
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Mechanical stewardship anchor for findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability.

scholarly_and_policy_anchors.title: Open Source Definition
scholarly_and_policy_anchors.project_use: Handoff anchor for redistribution, modification, non-discrimination, and license freedoms.

requirements: native-register mathematical source shelf
glossary separates observed anchors from proposed project usage
TeX/PDF visual and mechanical validation
native or near-native technical reviewer authority
machine-readable manifest with source coverage, files, hashes, gaps, and review state
no local claim of native acceptability without external review
each standard or register remains a separate sublane until cross-register rationale exists
shared and divergent terms are tracked separately
script, orthography, and transliteration are treated as governance decisions
review authority exists for each affected standard or register
family bridge may remain research before learner-facing publication
existing project authority is identified
design changes are logged as proposals
script sidecars are validated where script is part of accessibility
review packet separates community, linguist, and mathematical-register review
lane remains research or pilot until external review supports learner-facing use
explicit research question
no claim to represent a community
versioned grammar, morphology, script, lexicon, and mathematical register
translation samples marked as demonstrations
educational deployment requires opt-in users, teacher review, and rejection path
publication framing emphasizes method, auditability, and limits
local educational needs identified without speaking for local users
open licensing, local editability, and handoff paths recorded
CARE/TRUST-style authority review for minoritized or politically sensitive contexts
teacher/community feedback tracked separately from mechanical validation
downstream users retain authority to reject, fork, adapt, or own materials
reproducible corpus alignment, tokenization, model versions, and metrics
human review for any user-facing generated text
pivot is not treated as a language standard
publication claims limited to tooling, alignment, or evaluation unless reviewed human outputs exist

branches.condition: regional standard, dialect, register, or script variant
zonal or interlanguage project with existing community resources

decision_framework.name: match_evidence_to_claim
rules: mechanical claims can be handled locally
evidential claims require source shelves and page inspection
pedagogical claims require educator or learner review
canonical-edition claims require external native/technical review plus complete render/package validation

decision_framework.name: record_the_boundary
rules: every artifact says what it proves and does not prove
term anchors are not term approvals
open source is not community consent
successful build is not successful translation
constructed language can be a valid research object without being a valid canonical edition

publication_note: Frame semi-constructed and interlanguage work as methodological research under the translation header.
Ask how AI-assisted workflows can make technical-register construction auditable.
Use source shelves, term anchors, render manifests, and correction ledgers to separate machine-checkable claims from authority claims.
Treat interlanguage projects as existing communities and governance structures, not blank design spaces.
Treat low-resource educational translation through open-source handoff, not intervention.
Pair FAIR-style reproducibility with CARE/TRUST-style authority and ethics.
Name native/external review as a requirement, not an optional polish step.
